requirements.statement: The animals backend's stored notification record, the validation it applies at its API, its lifecycle writes and what it publishes carry only the additions other requirements in this area name: the facts, filters and sorts each set's own notification list needs, the templates store, the authorities' outcomes once they arrive, and the germinal products set's category held on the record only with its details and its trade-line codes. Everything else about the record, its API validation, its writes and its events is as the backend already has it, the submitted date and the flag saying whether a submitted notification's answers have since changed included.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows no persistence, API, event or PIMS behaviour, so the backend changes only where another area's requirement needs it to.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by the backend behaviour the requirements below record from repo:backend, repo:tests and trace:e2e. The backend already records the submitted date (repo-backend-p1-011, req-1499) and the answers-differ flag (repo-backend-p1-015, this area's own requirement for it). Each addition named is its own requirement: the templates store req-1310 (repo-backend-p2-123: no templates today), the authorities' outcomes req-1082, and the germinal products set's category, details and trade-line codes req-1884 to req-1895. The repo holds no rulings ledger of its own (repo-backend-p1-093). The outstanding items list this statement used to name is withdrawn by the 19 November ruling, and the status it used to name beside the four is withdrawn by the 16 November ruling; both withdrawals are recorded as this area's conflicts.

requirements.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection 'notification', with a database id, its identity and metadata (reference number, status, timestamps, fulfilments) at the document root and its answers nested under a notification sub-object, which holds no section beyond origin, commodities, reason for import, additional details, the five parties, CPH number, transport, purpose in the internal market, destination country, port of exit and exit date.
requirements.why: Every page reads and writes this one record, and the tests and the INS read model rely on its shape.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-001 to p1-003 (the notification collection, content sub-object and database id), repo-tests-p9-002 (the collection), p9-003 (one document per reference), p9-132 (the root fields) and p9-153 (the fifteen content sections the stored content may hold) show the shape today.

requirements.statement: A notification carries exactly one reference number, a string held at notification level rather than per commodity line, and it is unique across all notifications through a sparse unique index that lets records without a reference number coexist.
requirements.why: The reference number is how traders, PIMS and every endpoint find a notification, and one notification never carries two.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-004: the sparse unique index on the reference number. The V4 data fields page's Reference Number row says the same: a string that applies at notification level, one per notification and not driven by commodity selection (confluence-6497338582-p1-021, p1-026).

requirements.statement: The service, never the trader or any other caller, gives a new notification its reference number in the form GBN-AG-{YY}-{XXXXXX}: GBN for Great Britain Notification, AG for Animals and Germinals, YY the last two digits of the year the reference is allocated in, then a six-character Crockford base32 body (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O and U) drawn from a cryptographically secure source, for example GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P. A germinal products notification takes a GBN-AG reference like a live-animals one, so no GBN-GP reference exists.
requirements.why: References must be unguessable, readable aloud and unique per notification, and the AG in the prefix stands for Animals and Germinals, so one shape serves both sets.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-023 and p2-024 (ReferenceNumberGenerator's format and secure random source), p2-020 (create assigns the number) and p2-025 (one fixed GBN-AG prefix whatever the commodities) already meet it. The V4 data fields page's Reference Number row gives the same four parts, the same example and the same six-character Crockford base32 body, marks the field N/A for mandatory so no trader is asked for it (confluence-6497338582-p1-028-m1), and records that it impacts both the animals and the germinals journeys (p1-030). The page names no source for the value (p1-027), so the backend's own generation stands.

requirements.statement: When a generated reference number collides with an existing one, create tries a fresh number up to three times in all, then fails with a 500.
requirements.why: The generator does not guarantee a new number; the caller handles the clash.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-022: createNotification retries up to three times in all, then throws an IllegalStateException that the generic handler answers as 500.

requirements.statement: Every endpoint that takes a reference number in its path refuses one that does not match ^GBN-AG-\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$ with a 400 Validation Error before any lookup, its errors map keyed by referenceNumber.
requirements.why: A malformed reference is turned away before it reaches the store.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-008: the pattern on every path reference number in NotificationController, a violation answered as 400; p1-077: a method-parameter violation's errors map is keyed by the last segment of the property path.

requirements.statement: Every notification carries a concurrency token, returned in each response, that is its optimistic-lock version: it advances on each write, and a content save is checked against the token the caller sends, not the stored one, so a save without a token is refused with 400.
requirements.why: Two people or tabs editing one notification must not silently overwrite each other.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-006 (the concurrencyToken version field), p2-004 (every write returns the whole record), p2-010 (no token, 400) and p2-011 (the save is made at the caller's token).

requirements.statement: A save sent with a stale concurrency token changes nothing and answers 409 with title 'Stale Concurrency Token', code STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN and detail 'The record was modified by another request; refresh and try again.'; the first writer's change stands.
requirements.why: The second of two concurrent writers is told to refresh rather than losing the first writer's work.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-084 (GlobalExceptionHandler's stale-token answer) and p2-011 (a save at a stale token is refused as a conflict).

requirements.statement: Amend and cancel-amend take no concurrency token from the caller, so they act on the version stored when the call arrives; content saves, submit and copy each require the token the caller last read.
requirements.why: Records today's behaviour: the actions that change or send the content are checked against the version the user last saw.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-051: amend and cancel amend take no token; p2-042-m1: copy and submit refuse a request without the concurrencyToken query parameter; p2-010: a content save needs one.

requirements.statement: A notification has exactly one of four lifecycle statuses, DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND or DELETED, in the notification API and its fulfilments view alike, with no cancelled, rejected, in-progress or template status among them; any further status sits beside these four rather than replacing one of them.
requirements.why: Every lifecycle rule and every published event keys off these four values.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-008 (NotificationStatus) and repo-tests-p9-006 hold the four values today, p2-125 shows the service only ever moves a notification between them, and repo-tests-p9-004 and p9-042 show a draft and a two-commodity notification taking DRAFT and SUBMITTED. The one status this programme would have added beside them is withdrawn by the 16 November ruling, and 'Completed' waits for a real source of completion (req-1082).

requirements.statement: The server stamps created on creation and updated on every save and lifecycle change, as instants; a client cannot set the database id, created, updated, submittedAt or expireAt through a save request.
requirements.why: Audit times and expiry must not be forgeable by a caller.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-009 and p1-010: server-stamped created and updated that the inbound shape cannot carry; p1-053: the inbound notification carries only a reference number, a status, a concurrency token and the fulfilments beside its content; p2-018: updated is stamped on every write.

requirements.statement: submittedAt records the most recent submission: set to now on the first submit from DRAFT and on each re-submit from AMEND, left unchanged by starting or cancelling an amendment, and set by no other action.
requirements.why: PIMS and the dashboard show when the notification was last submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-011 and p1-011-m1 (the submittedAt field and what a submission records), p2-045 (stamped on a first submission and each resubmission) and p2-059 (cancelling an amendment keeps the original date).

requirements.statement: In a non-prod environment with NOTIFICATION_TTL_DAYS set, each new notification (copies included) gets an expireAt that many days after its created time, whatever its status later becomes; nothing (save, submit, amend) extends it; no expiry is stamped in prod (ENVIRONMENT 'prod' in any letter case, 'local' when unset) or when the setting is unset, and a value that is not positive is refused.
requirements.why: Test environments clear out old notifications without any risk to production data.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-112 and p2-113 (expiry stamped once, at creation, from created plus the configured days), p2-030 (a copy gets its own expiry), p2-115 to p2-117 (never in prod, prod matched in any case, days must be positive and are unset by default) and p2-119 (no days value set in the repo for any environment).

requirements.statement: Removal of expired notifications is switched on only where NOTIFICATION_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED is true (false by default): the backend then creates expiry indexes at start-up and the database removes each notification at its expiry time, and the backend refuses to create those indexes in prod even when removal is switched on.
requirements.why: Expiry must never run in prod, so production is protected twice: by no expiry being stamped and by no expiry index being made.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-114 (NotificationExpiryIndex creates expiry indexes at start-up when expiry is enabled), p2-115 (refused in prod) and p2-116 (NOTIFICATION_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED, false by default). The scheduled sweeper an earlier extraction recorded is gone from main.

requirements.statement: A notification of any status whose expiry time has passed is removed together with its accompanying documents; a notification with no expireAt is never removed by expiry.
requirements.why: Expired test data and its uploads are removed together.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-114: expired notifications and accompanying documents are removed by the database through expiry indexes; p2-113: the expiry applies whatever the status; p1-012: a record may carry no expireAt.

requirements.statement: Expiry writes no audit record and no outbox event, so other services are not told when a test notification expires.
requirements.why: Records today's behaviour: removal is done by the database, not by the service's lifecycle code.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-114: the database removes expired records through expiry indexes, so no service code runs; p2-104: only admin hard deletes and replays write an audit record.

requirements.statement: At start-up the backend logs whether new notifications get an expiry and, when they do not, why: prod, or no days set.
requirements.why: Operators can see whether expiry is in force in an environment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-118: NotificationExpiryStampingLog. The per-sweep log lines this used to record went with the sweeper, which main no longer has.

requirements.statement: expireAt and the pre-amend notification and fulfilment snapshots are never shown in any API response.
requirements.why: They are server-only state.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-012 and p1-014 (never returned in an API response) and p1-069 (the fulfilments view returns none of the server-only fields).

requirements.statement: The fulfilments payload (each obligation holding a single value or a list of records with their own fulfilment id and value) is stored exactly as sent and never interpreted by the backend, and date-shaped strings inside it, in plain text fields and in outbox data stay strings.
requirements.why: The frontend journey engine owns the fulfilment model and rehydrates the journey from it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-017 (opaque fulfilments), p1-061 (date-shaped strings stay strings) and repo-tests-p9-123 (the stored fulfilment entries).

requirements.statement: Starting an amendment stores independent deep copies of the notification content (inline parties as they stood included) and of the fulfilments payload; cancelling restores both, submitting the amendment clears both while keeping the edited content; a notification never amended, or submitted, holds no snapshot.
requirements.why: Cancel-amend must be able to restore exactly what was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-014 and p1-014-m1 (the two deep-copied snapshots), p1-072 (the content deep copy), p2-052 (opening an amendment stores them), p2-046 and p2-058 (submit and cancel clear them); repo-tests-p9-029 and trace-e2e-p14-130 show no snapshot after submit.

requirements.statement: Wherever the backend needs a notification's content, a record with no content sub-object fails at once, which the catch-all handler answers as a 500.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The claim it rested on left the working set when the backend was re-extracted, and the new extraction records only the record's shape (repo-backend-p1-002). The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.

requirements.statement: A save body (POST /notifications and PUT /notifications/{referenceNumber}) is a wrapper holding a required, validated notification object (content fields plus referenceNumber, status, concurrencyToken and fulfilments) and an optional actor; a body without notification is refused with 400 Validation Error naming notification.
requirements.why: The frontend sends this one shape for every save.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-052 and p2-003 (SaveNotificationDto with a required, validated notification and an optional actor), p1-053 (what the inbound notification carries) and p1-074 (the validation error shape).

requirements.statement: The backend enforces no rule on the notification's content: no required field, length or format on any section or free-text field (CPH number, email, phone, postcode, country code), and submit checks only the status and the concurrency token, not completeness. Every check a trader sees is the frontend journey's, which decides what a page must hold before it saves and what the notification must hold before it submits.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's validation is built in the frontend journey, the owner's rulings keep every page check there and apply it to both save buttons alike, and the backend accepts drafts at any depth.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-054 (no validation rule on any content field), p1-039 (nothing validates the country code's format) and p2-048 (no completeness check on submit) meet it. The owner's 26 October ruling and the 27 November ruling's answer on the save buttons put the same checks on both save buttons, the page's own hard stops plus whatever the data specification marks mandatory to proceed; those checks are the frontend's, so the backend's own validation does not change.

requirements.statement: The record's origin section holds the country of origin code, whether a region code is required (as the text 'yes' or 'no'), the region of origin code with its country prefix (for example FR-75), the country subdivision code and the trader's internal reference.
requirements.why: The origin page saves here and the GBN-AG payload reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-020 and p1-021 (Origin's five text values) and repo-tests-p9-007 to p9-010 / trace-e2e-p14-123 (stored FR, yes, FR-75, Imports456GB).

requirements.statement: The record holds a list of commodities, one per commodity the trader chose and empty by default, each with a name (the commodity's display name, such as 'Cattle' for 0102), a commodity code, a description, whole-number totals of animals and packages, and a list of species lines; each species line holds a species value, its display text and its common name, with its own whole-number number of animals and number of packages. Counts the frontend sends as strings are stored as numbers.
requirements.why: One notification can carry several commodity lines and species, each chosen species keeps its own counts, and PIMS receives a trade line per species.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-022 to p1-027 (the commodities list, Commodity and Species) and repo-tests-p9-011 to p9-016, p9-040 and p9-121 meet it; p2-013 stores an empty list when commodities are missing. The 27 November ruling keeps each species' own number of animals and packages, which the record already holds. The older commodity-complement shape a trace and the tests repo's API model still show is settled by c-514.

requirements.statement: Each species line holds a list of animal identifier units, one per animal (every unit kept), each with a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, free-text identification details, a description and a permanent address as a full party; an identifier the journey did not ask for is stored as an empty string or left out, and the two are treated alike. The line also keeps single ear tag, passport and microchip fields carrying its first unit.
requirements.why: PIMS needs each animal's identifiers, and records saved before per-animal identifiers still map.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-028 to p1-032 (Species and AnimalIdentifier) and repo-tests-p9-017, p9-018, p9-019 and p9-041; trace-e2e-p14-136 shows a missing and an empty passport stored the same way.

requirements.statement: The record holds the reason for import (for example internalMarket) and the purpose in the internal market (for example breeding) as text codes.
requirements.why: The import reason page saves here and the GBN-AG clauses read it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-033 and p1-049 (reasonForImport and purposeInInternalMarket as text) and repo-tests-p9-020, p9-021 (each stored as the answer's code).

requirements.statement: The record's additional details hold what the animals are certified for (a text code, for example slaughter) and whether there are unweaned animals (as the text 'yes' or 'no').
requirements.why: The additional details page saves here and the GBN-AG payload reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-034 (AdditionalDetails) and repo-tests-p9-022, p9-023 / trace-e2e-p14-126.

requirements.statement: The record holds five parties, each with an optional name, email, phone and address: placeOfOrigin, consignor, consignee, importer and destination; an unanswered role stores none of them, and the record holds no consignment contact.
requirements.why: The party pickers save here and the GBN-AG payload maps each role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-035 and p1-036 (the five parties and ConsignmentParty) and repo-tests-p9-025, p9-152 and p9-154 (five parties stored, no consignment contact) meet it. The consignment contact an older trace still shows stored is settled by c-515.

requirements.statement: Each party is stored as a literal copy of the address-book record picked for it, with no address id linking back, so later address-book edits or deletions never change the notification.
requirements.why: A submitted notification must keep what the trader declared.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-037 (a party is a literal copy); repo-tests-p9-024 and trace-e2e-p14-127-m1 prove no addressId is stored, and p9-028 reads each stored party back against the live address-book record.

requirements.statement: An address is a Standard Address Block named as the address book names it: address line 1, optional address line 2, town or city, optional county, postcode and an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (any country, not only the UK); there is no address line 3, city or free-text country.
requirements.why: Addresses copy across from the address book without translation and PIMS gets a country code.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-038 and p1-039 (Address) and repo-tests-p9-026 / trace-e2e-p14-128.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is stored as one text string, the county, parish and holding parts joined with no separator (12, 345, 6789 stored as '123456789').
requirements.why: The CPH page saves here and the GBN-AG final destination reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-040 (CPH number as text) and repo-tests-p9-030 / trace-e2e-p14-131 (stored unbroken).

requirements.statement: The record's transport section holds the port of entry (as the port's code), the arrival date, the means of transport, the transport identification, the transport document reference and the transited countries as country codes in the order added.
requirements.why: The arrival and transit pages save here and the GBN-AG transport movement reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-041 to p1-047 (Transport) and repo-tests-p9-031 to p9-034; trace-e2e-p14-132 stores FR then BE.

requirements.statement: The means of transport is one of AIRPLANE, RAILWAY, ROAD_VEHICLE or VESSEL; any other value is refused as a 400 Malformed Request.
requirements.why: PIMS needs a mode code for each value.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-045 (MeansOfTransport).

requirements.statement: The transport section holds one transporter with a name, an address, an approval number and a free-text type (for example 'Commercial') and no email or phone; it is not an address-book party.
requirements.why: The transporter page saves here and the GBN-AG carrier reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-048 (Transporter, its type free text) and repo-tests-p9-035, p9-036, p9-037.

requirements.statement: The record holds a destination country, a port of exit and an exit date (the calendar day chosen, sent as YYYY-MM-DD, with no time or zone).
requirements.why: The exit pages save here.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-050 and p1-051 and repo-tests-p9-133, which also records that no spec in that slice asserts the three fields. The 27 November ruling keeps the exit date question in live animals and asks none in germinal products, so a germinal record leaves the field empty.

requirements.statement: Every date-only field (arrival date, exit date, a document's date of issue and any added later) accepts only a plain date such as 2026-07-21; a value carrying a time or an offset is a 400 Malformed Request, never a 500 or a silently dropped time, and how moments are read does not change.
requirements.why: A calendar date must never shift by a day between the user's choice and PIMS.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-057 and p1-058 (StrictLocalDateModule) and p1-075 (the malformed-request answer).

requirements.statement: Calendar dates are stored as YYYY-MM-DD strings ('2026-07-21'), so they read back as the chosen date in any server time zone and sort in date order; moments (created, updated, submittedAt, expireAt and audit timestamps) are stored without a zone, to millisecond precision.
requirements.why: Fixes EUDPA-282, where UK summer time stored the previous day.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-059, p1-060 and p1-062 (LocalDateStringConverters and the design notes) and repo-tests-p9-038 / trace-e2e-p14-133.

requirements.statement: The API sends dates and moments as ISO-8601 strings, never epoch numbers or arrays, and its OpenAPI schema marks each calendar-date field as format date and each moment as format date-time.
requirements.why: Callers can parse every date the same way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-063 and p1-064 (the design notes on the API date contract).

requirements.statement: Every error the backend's exception handler answers is an RFC 7807 problem detail sent as application/problem+json, carrying the request's traceId when there is one.
requirements.why: Callers get one error shape and support can follow a request.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-073 (GlobalExceptionHandler and ProblemDetailsFactory).

requirements.statement: A body or parameter that fails validation gets 400 with type validation-error, title 'Validation Error', detail 'Validation failed for one or more fields' and an errors map from each failing field to its messages: a method-parameter violation keyed by the last segment of its property path, a missing required parameter mapped to 'Required request parameter is missing', and a parameter of the wrong type mapped to 'Request parameter has an invalid value'.
requirements.why: The caller can tell which fields failed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-074, p1-077, p1-078 and p1-079 (GlobalExceptionHandler's validation answers).

requirements.statement: A body that cannot be read gets 400 with type malformed-request, title 'Malformed Request' and detail 'Request body could not be read. Check the JSON is well-formed, that each date-only field is a date, for example 2026-12-12, and that each timestamp is an RFC 3339 instant, for example 2026-12-12T00:00:00Z'; the parser's own message is only logged.
requirements.why: The caller learns what to fix without the response echoing submitted values or internal types.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-075 and p1-076.

requirements.statement: A payload that binds but the application rejects, such as a callback missing required metadata, gets 400 with type bad-request, title 'Bad Request' and the refusal's own message as detail.
requirements.why: Lifecycle refusals reach the caller with their reason.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-080 (BadRequestException handling).

requirements.statement: A missing resource gets 404 with type not-found, title 'Resource Not Found' and the refusal's message as detail; a missing notification's message is 'Cannot find notification with reference number: ' followed by the reference.
requirements.why: One not-found shape for every endpoint.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-082 (the 404 handler) and p2-084 (the not-found message).

requirements.statement: An upstream failure (unreachable, timed out or non-2xx) gets 502 with title 'Upstream Service Error' and the exception's message as detail.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The backend's exception handler on main has no upstream-error answer, and the claim this rested on left the working set when the backend was re-extracted; today the handler's answers are those repo-backend-p1-073 to p1-086 record. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-073: today's handler and its problem-detail answers, none of them a 502.

requirements.statement: A resource conflict such as a duplicate key gets 409 with type conflict, title 'Resource Conflict' and the refusal's message as detail.
requirements.why: One conflict shape for duplicate writes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-083 (ConflictException handling).

requirements.statement: An oversized upload gets 413 with title 'Payload Too Large' and detail 'Uploaded file exceeds the maximum permitted size'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The backend's exception handler on main has no payload-too-large answer, and the claim this rested on left the working set when the backend was re-extracted. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-073: today's handler and its problem-detail answers, none of them a 413.

requirements.statement: A failure to write the outbox event, or to get a notification's write lock after two retries 50 milliseconds apart, gets 500 with title 'Internal Server Error' and detail 'An error occurred during submission. Please try again.', whichever lifecycle action failed.
requirements.why: The user is asked to retry without internal detail leaking.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-085 (the outbox-write answer), p2-019 (the lock gives up after two retries with 500) and p2-120 (50 milliseconds between tries).

requirements.statement: Any other unexpected runtime failure gets 500 with title 'Internal Server Error' and detail 'An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.'; Spring's own framework errors, such as an unknown path, keep Spring's default answers (for example 404).
requirements.why: Unexpected faults never leak internals and unknown paths are not turned into 500s.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-086 and p1-087.

requirements.statement: The backend listens on port 8085, writes a notification and its outbox event in one MongoDB transaction, so MongoDB runs as a replica set, and serves Swagger UI in the local profile only.
requirements.why: Records the runtime the record depends on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-088 (README: port and replica set) and p2-132 (Swagger UI off in deployed environments, on locally). The Floci provisioning and start-up settings an earlier extraction recorded are no longer in this area's working set.

requirements.statement: The backend README describes its tests accurately.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a documentation inaccuracy the DR2.1 goal does not cover, which goes to the report. The claim that the README calls the tests mock-free while a test uses Mockito left the working set when the backend was re-extracted; repo-backend-p1-093 is what the new extraction says of the README. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-093: the README, AGENTS.md and design notes give reasons, not rulings.

requirements.statement: POST /notifications with no reference number creates a notification: its created time stamped, its organisation set from the organisation header, a new reference number, status DRAFT, every sent field stored and returned, and a NotificationCreated outbox event at aggregate version 1; in the live-animals frontend a post to the set's notifications path redirects to the new notification's origin page.
requirements.why: Starting a notification creates the record the journey then fills.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-001, p2-002, p2-020 and p2-021 (create), p4-004 and p4-019 (the NotificationCreated event, versions starting at 1) and repo-tests-p9-064, p9-131.

requirements.statement: Every save and lifecycle endpoint answers 200 with the whole stored notification record, and no endpoint returns the inbound notification shape.
requirements.why: The frontend picks up the new concurrency token and state from each write.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-004 and p1-070.

requirements.statement: A content save replaces the whole notification content (origin, commodities, reason for import, additional details, the five parties, CPH number, transport, purpose in internal market, destination country, port of exit, exit date and the fulfilments payload), so a field left out of the body is saved as empty rather than merged, keeps the status, creates no second notification and writes a NotificationEdited event.
requirements.why: Each page save sends the whole record built from the journey.

requirements.statement: Every call the end-to-end suite makes to the notification API carries an API key in an x-api-key header where one is configured, which is required when the suite runs against a CDP environment from outside it; a submit or amend is tried at most three times when the backend answers 500, waiting 500 then 1000 milliseconds, and any rate-limited call is retried up to three times, honouring a Retry-After header where one is given and waiting at most five seconds, or 1, 2 and then 4 seconds without one.
requirements.why: The outbox lock a submission takes can be held transiently, so a server error on submit is not a failure of the record; and the suite has to reach a CDP environment's API the way any other client does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-127 (the x-api-key header), p9-128-m1 (submit and amend retried on a 500), and p9-129 and p9-129-m1 (rate-limited calls retried) are the suite's behaviour today.

requirements.statement: A notification created and submitted through an intercepting security proxy is still submitted, so the submit path holds up under an active security scan.
requirements.why: Submission is the one action that leaves the service, so it is the path the security scan has to clear.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-130: the one backend security test submits through the local scanning proxy and reads back Submitted.

requirements.statement: Deleting a submitted notification deactivates its PIMS Dynamics record.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the animals backend already publishes the deletion event, but the dynamics gateway's allow-list drops it, so nothing reaches PIMS, and how PIMS should record a deleted notification is not settled. Both sit with the PIMS mapping work rather than this programme, and they go to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-095: the gateway's allow-list drops the deletion event; p9-096: the suite guesses at an Inactive state and status reason.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-139 records the eight commodity lines under four codes the suite exercises, and p9-141 and p9-142 the identifiers it holds the journey to; both are fixtures of the suite rather than the specification.

requirements.why: Out of scope: the fixture's flat summary is stale test data in the tests repo rather than a Design Release 2.1 difference, and no spec reads it, so correcting it is not part of this programme; it goes to the report.

requirements.statement: Each notification holds a flag saying whether its answers differ from the answers it was submitted with, always yes or no, never empty: no on a new notification and on a record stored without it, worked out again on each content save during an amendment from the notification content alone (uploaded documents and the fulfilments payload never count, and an answer put back reads as unchanged), no for an amendment with no stored submitted version, and reset to no when the amendment is submitted or cancelled. The fulfilments view returns it, and it is not published on any notification event.
requirements.why: The view tells the trader whether an amendment has changed anything before they resubmit, and the owner's 19 November ruling makes the flag a non-null yes or no that the backend's shape owns and the frontend's stub copies.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-015 and p1-016 (answersDifferFromSubmitted, always true or false), p2-014 to p2-016 (worked out on each amendment save over the notification fields), p2-046 and p2-058 (reset on submit and cancel), p1-069 (the fulfilments view returns it) and p4-174 (not published in the GBN-AG body).

requirements.statement: A notification only ever moves between four statuses: DRAFT on create, SUBMITTED on submit or cancel amend, AMEND on amend and DELETED on soft delete. A DELETED notification cannot be saved, submitted, amended or copied, and a SUBMITTED notification's content cannot be saved until it is moved to AMEND.
requirements.why: Every page and every published event relies on the lifecycle moving only along these paths.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-125 (every status change the service makes), p2-126 and p2-127 (what DELETED and SUBMITTED refuse), and each operation's allowed statuses: p2-009 save, p2-027 copy, p2-042 submit, p2-050 amend, p2-056 cancel amend, p2-061 and p2-063 soft delete.

requirements.statement: Every trader notification route, and every document-uploads route bar the scan-result callbacks, scopes the record to the organisation named in the caller's Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and refuses a request without a non-blank one with 400 and the detail 'Missing required header Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id'; a new notification belongs to the organisation in the header at creation, and the organisation recorded on an event and its actor is that organisation.
requirements.why: One organisation's traders see and change only that organisation's notifications.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-005, p1-089, p2-085, p2-086 and p2-088 (TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter and the stored organisation), p4-022 (the event's organisationId) and repo-tests-p9-126 (every call names the organisation).

conflicts.about: Whether a notification's category travels on its outbox event, with an optional property in trade-imports-schemas for the INS backend, or stays on the notification record only.

positions.says: The category is stored on the notification record and is not published; trade-imports-schemas does not change in this programme.
c-272 is not needed in this programme.
Every INS read-model reader of the category is now blocked or moved to the animals frontend, which reads the category from the animals backend's own record.
Until the INS dashboard is re-distilled, today's INS table lists germinal notifications without their category.
c-272 is reopened when the INS dashboard area is re-distilled.
The category is published on the notification event the INS backend reads.
INS takes a notification's category from the event's category field, otherwise treating it as live animals.
No new PIMS profile version is made, so neither trade-imports-schemas nor trade-imports-dynamics-gateway changes for the germinal set.
Today an outbox event carries only an aggregate id, aggregate type, sub-type, aggregate version, event type, timestamp, data and metadata, with an actor and status changes beside them.
Today the GBN-AG body and the event envelope carry no notification category.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling, which ranks first, withdraws the earlier ruling's event half: the category is stored on the notification record (req-1884) and is not published on any outbox event, the event envelope stays exactly as today (req-1567, as repo-tests-p9-106 and repo-backend-p4-178 show it), and neither trade-imports-schemas nor trade-imports-dynamics-gateway changes in this programme. req-1887 is out of scope. Known gap: until the INS dashboard is re-distilled, today's INS table lists germinal notifications without their category; this conflict is reopened then. ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-032 and p1-033 are overruled; p1-043 still stands and agrees with the outcome.

conflicts.about: Whether GBN-AG trade lines carry a typeCode.

positions.says: Live-animal trade lines carry typeCode LIVE_ANIMAL.
Each germinal trade line carries the GBN-AG typeCode for what it is: SEMEN, EMBRYO or OVA.
Trade line items carry no typeCode: the record has no such field.
Until the MDM catalogue separates embryos from ova, today's germinal lines carry interim typeCodes.
Semen lines carry the typeCode SEMEN.
Today's combined 'Embryos/Ova' lines carry the typeCode EMBRYO by default.
EMBRYO and OVA become separate items only once the catalogue is re-distilled.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings outrank the backend: live-animal lines gain typeCode LIVE_ANIMAL (req-1894). Until the MDM catalogue separates embryos from ova, semen lines carry SEMEN and today's combined 'Embryos/Ova' lines carry EMBRYO by default (req-1928); OVA as its own code, with embryos and ova as separate lines, applies once the catalogue is re-distilled (req-1800). repo-backend-p4-177 is not overruled because it is the evidence of today's behaviour those requirements change. ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-036 is not overruled: the afternoon ruling defers its OVA half until the catalogue is re-distilled rather than withdrawing it.

INS takes a notification's category from the event's category field, and otherwise treats it as live-animals.
The category is stored on the notification record and is not published on the notification event.
c-272 is reopened when the INS dashboard area is re-distilled.

How the category reaches the INS read model is decided when the INS dashboard is re-distilled. The morning ruling's event publishing and INS's reading of it are overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether submitting records the outstanding items left at that moment.

positions.says: The animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list and the rule that works it out, both re-added later with the outstanding-actions banner, while the submitted date is still recorded; this replaces the 16 November ruling's 'what stays' clause on the outstanding items.
Submitting a notification records the outstanding items left at the moment of submission, because a future banner needs them.
Submitting a notification records the date it was submitted.

conflicts.outcome: The 19 November ruling is the later word and ranks first: the notification record keeps the submitted date and holds no outstanding items list, and the rule that works them out comes off the outstanding-item enum (req-909, req-2385). Both are re-added with the outstanding-actions banner (req-2334). The 16 November claim that submitting records the outstanding items is overruled; its claim that submitting records the date is carved out of the supersession and still stands.

conflicts.about: Whether submitting a notification records the outstanding items left at the moment of submission.

positions.says: The animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list, the health-certificate-owed list that nothing reads, and the rule that works it out comes off the outstanding-item type; both are re-added later with the future outstanding-actions banner.
This call replaces the 16 November ruling's clause that kept the outstanding items, so that ruling no longer keeps them; only the submitted date stays.
Submitting a notification records the outstanding items left at the moment of submission, because a future banner needs them.

conflicts.outcome: The 19 November ruling is the later word and ranks above the 16 November one, and it names the clause it replaces, so the record holds no outstanding items list and nothing derives one from the outstanding-item type; the backend already stores nothing about what is still owed (repo-backend-p1-011-m1). The submitted date is carved out of the supersession and is still recorded (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-024, met by req-1499). The list and its rule come back with the outstanding-actions banner, whose trigger neither ruling names. ruling-sam-2026-11-16-p1-011 is overruled; the same ruling's submitted-date claim p1-010 is not, because it still backs what is kept.

conflicts.about: Whether a 'Submitted action required' status is added beside the four lifecycle statuses.

positions.says: No new 'Submitted action required' status is introduced, and the 9 October afternoon ruling's status is withdrawn.

A notification submitted with outstanding items, such as a missing health certificate, has the status SUBMITTED like any other, because a status that does not align with the notification flow is not introduced.
Outstanding actions are shown through a banner-style alert the dashboard designs under test introduce, and nothing action-required is shown until that design lands.
The add-only status rule covers 'Submitted action required' and, once unblocked, 'Completed'.
A new status is mirrored in plants only where plants has the same lifecycle, and 'Submitted action required' rests on the ITAHC and is animals only.

conflicts.outcome: The 16 November ruling ranks above the 9 October afternoon one: no 'Submitted action required' status is added, so the enum stays at DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND and DELETED (req-1497, req-1987), a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other, and outstanding actions wait for the banner design. Neither p2-071 nor p2-076 is overruled, because each still backs something true: p2-071's add-only rule still covers 'Completed' once a real source of completion exists, and p2-076's rule that a status is mirrored in plants only where plants has the same lifecycle stands whatever the status is. The 'Action required' tag the same 16 November ruling withdraws from the live-animals list is the notification-list area's to record.

conflicts.about: How the 'answers differ from submitted' flag is held on the notification and whether it is exposed outside the service.

positions.says: 'Answers differ from submitted' is a non-null yes or no flag, and the animals frontend's local stub takes it from the backend's shape rather than working it out itself.
The ruling names neither the flag's field, nor its value for a notification that has never been submitted, nor whether it is published on the notification event.
Each record has an answersDifferFromSubmitted flag that is always true or false, false on a new notification and read as false on a record stored without it.
The fulfilments view returns answersDifferFromSubmitted, and the GBN-AG body does not publish it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and gives the flag's shape to the backend, and the backend on main now has that shape: a root-level answersDifferFromSubmitted flag that is always true or false, false on a new notification and on a record stored without it, returned on the fulfilments view and not published on any event (req-2865). That fills every point the ruling left open in the way the earlier default proposed, so nothing waits on the owner. No claim is overruled: the ruling's claims and the backend's agree.

The canned submission event the suite keeps carries a flat summary of the notification, with an eventId and a publishedAt the event model does not carry.
